text: To be baffled is to be completely puzzled by something you cannot explain, even after trying hard. It is stronger than confused: a baffled person has looked closely and still has no answer. Scientists were baffled because some chum salmon carry genes far more different from their neighbours' than anyone could account for.

A relic is something left over from an earlier time that is still around today. It can be an object, like a rusty sword in a museum, but it works just as well for a habit that only makes sense once you know where it came from. The salmon's odd spawning habits are relics of the years they spent trapped in ice-age lakes.

To speculate is to form an idea by reasoning from clues, without yet having proof. It is more than a wild guess, because a speculation is built to be tested. Martin speculated that the odd salmon had been trapped in glacial lakes, then gathered a team to check.

To thrive is to do very well, growing strong and healthy. Mammoths and sabre-toothed cats thrived in the ice age, and the surprise of the article is that some trapped salmon thrived too, instead of dying out as everyone assumed.

An ice age is a long stretch of time, thousands of years, when Earth is cold enough for huge sheets of ice called glaciers to cover much of the land. The last one ended roughly 12,000 years ago. This article is about the salmon that were caught in it.

To be inconvenienced is to have your plans made harder or more awkward. The writer is being playful: the ice age was a lot worse than a mild bother for salmon that suddenly could not reach the rivers they needed.

Chum salmon are one of the main kinds of Pacific salmon, found all around the northern Pacific from Japan to Oregon. They are born in rivers, grow up in the sea, and swim back into fresh water to lay their eggs. Chum has nothing to do with the word for a friend here, though the subheading plays on it.

When fish spawn, they lay their eggs. A spawning ground is the patch of river where a species does it, year after year. Salmon eggs need cold fresh water, so a salmon that cannot reach its spawning ground cannot have young at all.
Icebound means sealed shut or blocked by ice. During the ice age, glaciers froze the rivers that salmon used to travel between the sea and their spawning grounds, so the rivers were icebound.

A nuisance is something annoying that gets in your way but is not a disaster. For salmon that were out at sea when the ice came, a blocked river was only a nuisance, because they could go and find another river.
Accessible means easy to reach or get into. The salmon at sea looked for more accessible fresh water, meaning rivers and lakes that were not frozen shut.
Marine means to do with the sea. The marine part of a salmon's life is the years it spends out in the ocean growing big, between hatching in a river and returning to spawn.

A life-cycle is the full set of stages a living thing goes through, from birth to having young of its own. For salmon that means river, then sea, then river again. Scientists assumed that fish who could not complete the sea stage would die out.

Quaternary Research is a scientific journal, a magazine where scientists publish their studies. The Quaternary is the name geologists give to the most recent period of Earth's history, the last 2.6 million years, which includes the ice ages.

Avid means extremely keen and enthusiastic about something. An avid fisherman is someone who fishes as often as he possibly can, which is how Patrick Martin came to notice that some salmon were behaving strangely.

A sideline here is not the edge of a sports field. It means a second activity you do alongside your main job, the way someone might have a sideline selling cookies. Martin's sideline was science: he was not a professional researcher.

An amateur does something for love rather than as a paid job. An amateur scientist has no university post, but as Martin shows, an amateur can still ask a question the professionals missed and go on to answer it.
Employed here does not mean given a job. It is the other sense of the word: used. The study employed genetics, meaning it used the study of genes as its tool.

Genetics is the science of genes, the coded instructions inside every cell that are passed from parents to their young. Two fish that are genetically different carry different versions of those instructions, and comparing genes lets scientists work out which populations are closely related.
When animals range around an area, they live and roam across all of it. Chum salmon range around the whole rim of the Pacific, from Japan across to Alaska and down to Oregon.
A rim is an outer edge, like the rim of a cup. The Pacific rim is the ring of coastlines around the Pacific Ocean, and chum salmon live all the way around it.
An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea that reaches into the land. Cook inlet in Alaska is one of the three places where the salmon's genes turned out to be unusually different.

The Salish sea is the sheltered stretch of ocean between Vancouver Island in Canada and the coast of Washington state, including the waters around Seattle. Its chum salmon spawn in summer, unlike almost all others.

Something intriguing makes you curious and want to know more. To intrigue someone is to catch their interest that way. The intriguing twist is that the odd salmon do not just have different genes, they also behave differently.

To migrate is to travel a long way from one place to another, usually at the same time each year. Salmon migrate from the sea back into rivers to lay their eggs, a journey that can run hundreds of kilometres upstream.

Isolation means being cut off and kept apart from everyone else. To isolate a group is to seal it off. Biologists know that when a population of animals is isolated for thousands of years, it slowly becomes different from the group it was separated from.

Evolution is the slow change of living things over many generations, as small differences in genes build up. Something evolutionary has to do with that process. Being trapped in a lake sent the salmon down their own evolutionary path.

The Galápagos are a group of islands in the Pacific, far off the coast of Ecuador. Because animals there were cut off from the mainland, many evolved into forms found nowhere else, which is what made Charles Darwin famous for studying them.

A glacier is a huge, slow-moving river of ice that forms where snow piles up faster than it melts. Glacial means made or shaped by glaciers. A glacial lake is one that forms when a glacier blocks a valley and water backs up behind the ice.

A hunch is a strong feeling that something is true before you have proof. Martin's hunch was that the strange salmon had survived the ice age in lakes, and instead of leaving it as a feeling, he tested it.
To convene a group is to bring people together for a shared job or meeting. Martin convened a team of fish experts and rock experts from a university and a government agency to test his idea.
An ichthyologist is a scientist who studies fish. The word comes from ichthys, the ancient Greek for fish. The silent-looking start is said ik-thee-OL-uh-jist.
A geologist is a scientist who studies rocks, land and how Earth's surface changes over time. Martin needed geologists to work out where ice-age glaciers had dammed valleys and created lakes.

The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, usually called NOAA, is the United States government agency that studies the oceans and the weather. It also keeps track of fish populations, which is why its scientists joined the salmon study.
To analyse something is to examine it closely and carefully, piece by piece, to understand it. The team analysed the genes of tens of thousands of salmon. Analyse is the British spelling of analyze.
A specimen is one example of something, collected so it can be studied. Here each specimen was a single salmon whose genes were tested, and the team had 32,817 of them.

In biology a population is not just people. It is any group of one species living in one area and breeding together. The 310 salmon populations in the study were groups from 310 different rivers and coasts.

Cousins here is not about family in the usual sense. Scientists call two groups of the same species cousins when they are related but have been apart for a while, like the salmon of Asia and the salmon of North America.
Aberrant means different from what is normal or expected, straying from the usual pattern. The aberrant salmon populations are the ones whose genes and habits do not match the rest.

Bore here is the past tense of bear, meaning to carry or to have. To bear no close relation to something is to have no close connection to it. The odd salmon bore no close relation to Asian salmon, so mixing with Asian fish could not explain their genes.
Kin means relatives, the members of your family. The article uses it for the salmon's relatives across the ocean in Asia.

forms: went their own sweet evolutionary ways
text: To go your own sweet way is to do exactly as you please, without caring what anyone else is doing. The trapped salmon went their own sweet evolutionary way, changing in whatever direction suited their lake with no other salmon to blend back in with.
A chum is an old-fashioned word for a close friend. The subheading is a pun: these are chum salmon, and all chums together sounds like a gang of pals.

To rejig something is to rearrange or adjust it so it works in a new way. The trapped salmon rejigged their behaviour, treating the lake as their ocean and the streams feeding it as their spawning rivers.
To persist is to keep going or keep existing long after you might have expected it to stop. The new habits persisted even after the ice melted and the fish could reach the sea again.

An ice dam is a wall of glacier ice that blocks a valley the way a concrete dam blocks a river, so water piles up behind it into a lake. When the climate warmed and the ice dams melted, the lakes drained and the trapped salmon were released into the sea.
To be liberated is to be set free. Once the ice dams melted, the salmon were liberated from their lakes and could swim out to the ocean again.
A peculiarity is an odd or unusual feature that sets something apart. The salmon's genetic peculiarities are the unusual bits of their genes that other chum salmon do not have.
Presumably means probably, as far as anyone can reasonably tell. Writers use it to say something is very likely true without claiming it is proven.
Physiological means to do with how a living body works: breathing, digesting, dealing with salt and cold. A physiological adaptation is a change in how the body runs, rather than in how it looks.

An adaptation is a change in a living thing that helps it survive in its surroundings. Salmon that spent generations in fresh water may have developed adaptations to cope with it, and some of those may still be in their genes today.
To be confined is to be kept inside a limited space and unable to leave. The salmon were confined to fresh water for thousands of years by the ice.
Briny means salty, and the briny is an old, slightly jokey name for the sea. Chum salmon normally spend most of their lives in the briny, so being stuck in fresh water was a big change.
A conservationist is someone who works to protect wild animals, plants and the places they live. Conservationists care about these salmon because unusual populations add variety to the species.

Genetic diversity is how much variety there is in the genes across a species. A species with lots of diversity is safer, because if a disease or a change in climate wipes out fish with one set of genes, others with different genes may survive. That is why the article calls it insurance against extinction.
To have something in spades is to have a great deal of it. The odd salmon populations have genetic diversity in spades, meaning far more than usual.

A pathogen is any germ that causes disease, such as a virus or harmful bacteria. Fish farms in the sea struggle with pathogens and sea lice, which is why farmers might be interested in raising salmon in lakes instead.
Sea lice are tiny creatures that cling to the skin of salmon and feed on them, weakening the fish. They are a big problem for salmon farms in the ocean but are absent from freshwater lakes.
